newsitem.title: USA: Black church leader denies affair.
newsitem.headline: Black church leader denies affair.

text.p: The leader of the nation's largest black church group denied Friday he was having an affair with his business partner and said he was being slandered by local media reports.

Rev. Henry Lyons, president of the 8.5 million-member National Baptist Convention, USA, has been subject to intense scrutiny since his wife was arrested Sunday on charges she set fire to a $700,000 house he co-owns with Bernice Edwards.
"I want to catagorically deny that Bernice Edwards and I were carrying on an affair," Lyons told a news conference at the Bethel Metropolitan Baptist Church, where he has been minister for 25 years.
Deborah Lyons was by her husband's side as he spoke but did not speak herself. Edwards, whom Lyons said served as his executive secretary, was not present.

In an interview with the St. Petersburg Times published Tuesday, Mrs. Lyons said the fire was an accident and denied she acted because she believed her husband and Edwards were having an affair. Police are still investigating the fire, which caused an estimated $30,000 in damage.
Lyons refused to take questions from reporters after his statement. He said he would only answer questions from members of his church and the National Baptist Convention.
In his statement, he said the house was used for guests of the convention but did not say how it was paid for.
"I am concerned about my reputation. I have been slandered," he said. He added that he would work with his attorneys to restore the good names of his wife and himself.
Lyons said the Times and other local white-owned media had trouble recognising that blacks could be successful.

Lyons has close ties to President Clinton, who spoke at convention meetings in 1994 and 1996. First lady Hillary Rodham Clinton spoke at the church last year during her husband's re-election campaign.
